parameters.content:
## Turn long videos in Google Drive into captioned vertical clips

Drop a long video into a watched Drive folder. CNAPS Studio transcribes it, picks
the moments that stand on their own, cuts on word boundaries, reframes to
1080x1920 and burns in word-synced captions. Clips land in Drive, get logged in a
Sheet and announced in Slack — for podcasts, webinars and interviews that need
Shorts cuts filed and tracked.

Comparable pipelines chain four vendors. This uses one platform plus your own Gemini key.

### How it works
1. The trigger fires on a new file; a Code node sizes the wait from its duration.
2. Three HTTP calls open an MCP session, get an upload slot and POST the file.
3. An agent starts the CNAPS Studio flow, a Wait node sleeps, a second agent reads the result.
4. Each clip is downloaded to Drive, logged in the sheet and posted to Slack.

### Setup steps
1. Get a CNAPS Studio API key at cnaps.ai under API Key; the free plan can issue one.
2. Create an n8n Header Auth credential: name `x-api-key`, value that key.
3. In CNAPS Studio, add a Google Gemini API key under provider settings — Video Analysis runs on it. Get one at aistudio.google.com/apikey.
4. Add Anthropic (or OpenAI), Google Drive, Google Sheets and Slack credentials.
5. On the trigger, pick the Drive folder to watch.
6. In Settings, set `output_folder_id` (must differ from the watched folder), `sheet_id` and `slack_channel`.
7. Sheet headers: Source video, Clip, Title, Span, Duration (s), Camera, Drive link.

Needs n8n 1.104.0 or later.

### Customization
- `clip_instruction` decides what counts as a good moment.
- `clip_target_len_sec` and `tempo` control length and pacing.
- Swap Slack for email or Discord without touching anything upstream.

nodes.name: Section 4 - File each clip and report

parameters.content:
## 4. File every clip and report back

**One row per clip** flattens the list. The loop downloads each clip, saves it to
Drive and appends a sheet row. Slack gets one digest, or a message naming what failed.

nodes.name: Section 3 - Run it, then read it back

parameters.content:
## 3. Run the clip pipeline, then read it back

The first agent calls `create_flow` once. Transcription, moment selection,
word-boundary cuts, reframing and captions all happen inside CNAPS Studio.
**Wait** sleeps for the time from step 1, then **Check the run** reads the flow once.

nodes.name: Section 2 - Hand the video to CNAPS

parameters.content:
## 2. Hand the video to CNAPS

Three plain HTTP calls, no agent: open an MCP session, ask for a one-time upload
slot, then POST the file to it. The video is streamed straight from Drive.

nodes.name: Section 1 - Watch Drive and size the wait

parameters.content:
## 1. Watch Drive and size the wait

The trigger fires on a new file. **Settings** holds every value you change, so
nothing is hard-coded downstream. **Work out how long to wait** sizes the wait from
the video's duration and fails fast if the output folder is the watched one.

### Setup: folder to watch

Open this node and pick the Drive folder
that long videos get dropped into.

### Setup: fill in Settings

- `output_folder_id` must be a different folder from the one watched
- `sheet_id` / `sheet_name` point at the log spreadsheet
- `slack_channel` is where the digest goes

### Setup: CNAPS credential

Both HTTP nodes use one Header Auth
credential: name `x-api-key`, value your
CNAPS Studio API key. The free plan can
issue one.

nodes.name: Why there is no AI here

parameters.content:
### Why there is no AI here

The upload URL is a 64-character secret. One character
changed by a model gives a URL that looks right and 404s,
so it is read out of the response with a regex instead.

### Setup: model and MCP

Swap Anthropic Chat Model for any chat
model you have a credential for.

CNAPS MCP: endpoint `https://mcp.cnaps.ai/mcp`,
transport HTTP Streamable, auth Header Auth.

The Gemini key for Video Analysis goes in
CNAPS Studio, not here.

### Setup: sheet headers

Source video, Clip, Title, Span, Duration (s), Camera, Drive link

### If no clips come back

The Wait usually expired before the render finished. Raise
`wait_minutes_per_source_minute` or `max_wait_minutes` in Settings.

If the run never started, check for a Gemini key in CNAPS Studio.
